key_insight: This perspective argues that “AI-ready” biological data is not a vague label but a question of whether data are truly usable, interoperable, and trustworthy for machine learning. The paper frames readiness through four core questions that help define what good biological data should look like for AI.
problem_solved: Biological datasets are often fragmented, noisy, poorly standardized, and difficult for AI systems to reuse effectively. The paper addresses the lack of a clear framework for deciding when biological data are actually ready for AI workflows.
method: Frames AI-readiness as a set of four guiding questions for biological data assessment.
Uses a conceptual/model perspective rather than proposing a new algorithm or benchmark.
Emphasizes data quality, context, provenance, and usability as criteria for evaluating readiness.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a practical way to judge whether biological data can support reliable model training and interpretation. It can improve dataset selection, reduce hidden biases, and support more robust biological discovery.
visual_elements: A four-part framework diagram showing the four questions around “AI-ready data”.
A pipeline illustration from raw biological data to AI-ready data to model outputs.
Icons for data quality, metadata/provenance, interoperability, and trustworthiness.
A checklist-style infographic showing readiness criteria with pass/fail indicators.
paper_title: Four questions for AI-ready biological data
